question: Does interpreting the automatic cerebrum object as all removable material suppress supplied-target progress, compared with an explicit simulated occupancy assumption that also includes the supplied tumor?

source_evidence.finding: ReMIND distinguishes automatic Brainlab Elements Object Manipulation cerebrum from manual whole tumor and prescribed tumor target. Enhancing tumor includes any necrotic core. Software version and per-case object generation order are not given.
source_evidence.scope: exact dataset methods, not physical occupancy validation

source_evidence.document: Brainlab iPlan Stereotaxy 3.0 Software User Guide, Revision 1.4, copyright 2014
source_evidence.section: 13.4 Creating Objects Using Automatic Segmentation / Outlining Tumors
source_evidence.paraphrase: Automatic structures exclude a previously outlined tumor region; the PDF spells the verb substract.
source_evidence.finding: The atlas objects include cerebrum, gray and white matter. The guide recommends outlining tumor first; without that outline the tumor is ignored during segmentation. Outline errors propagate to automatic objects.
source_evidence.scope: manufacturer-authored historical workflow evidence; hosted mirror; not proof that ReMIND Elements used this exact version or procedure

notation.S: unchanged automatic cerebrum label on qualified planning grid
notation.T: unchanged full supplied whole-tumor positive region
notation.required: T is contained in D; public support source domain covers the existing crop; all original file and cohort bindings remain valid
notation.baseline_upper_bound: For any removal R subset S, |R intersect T| / |T| <= |S intersect T| / |T|; this ignores additional tool and access restrictions

conditions.assumption: Every positive supplied-tumor voxel is treated as occupied removable material for this rigid-cell research world, including any unseparated necrotic component. This is not measured material composition, viable tumor, surgical indication, or corrected anatomy.
forbidden_operations: occupancy inferred from bright MRI signal
conditions.outside_union: Unchanged zeros retain baseline simulation interpretation, not certified air, CSF or safe corridor. Anatomy outside source domains/crop remains unknown.
conditions.proof_not_claimed: physical correctness or feasibility of complete target removal

pairing.raw_MRI: same exact samples and source/grid provenance
pairing.target: same T and D with full original |T| denominator in both conditions
pairing.access: derive once from raw S and T with existing fixed axis0 rule; freeze the same world-space aperture/axis/radius for both arms, rather than rerunning access selection on the union
pairing.tools_and_geometry: unchanged canonical generic tools, shaft clearance, contained-cell removal, temporal ordering and grid reconciliation
pairing.task: same reward, max_steps 24, proposal cap120, depth-volume proposal family and public global target context variant as existing TRAIN condition
pairing.models: none in this diagnostic; no checkpoint loads, learning, gradients or optimizer calls
pairing.observation_caveat: Existing support-percentile MRI normalization depends on occupancy. Record any A/B normalization change; no neural-policy comparison is permitted until normalization is explicitly shared or the coupled change is declared. Raw MRI remains unchanged.
pairing.identity: separate immutable source/model/context hashes per condition; exact baseline hashes must reconstruct; derived provenance binds both original masks, operation and added-cell digest

proposed_bounded_run_after_source_review.sequence: For each fixed TRAIN case, construct A then B sequentially, record complete initial inventories, run existing observed_greedy_search with identical limits, and replay each completed returned sequence under its own exact world. Release each arm before the next.
proposed_bounded_run_after_source_review.outputs: compact metadata/inventories/decision and replay ledgers only; no duplicate arrays or images
proposed_bounded_run_after_source_review.failure_policy: Retain all eight planned rows including source/access/cap failures; global resource refusal terminates remaining work with explicit not-run rows; capped searches remain unresolved, never accepted as complete STOP; no automatic retry or SELECT-driven condition choice.
metrics: S, T, S intersect T and T minus S counts

minimal_implementation_gaps_before_run: Add one explicit TRAIN-only occupancy-condition seam to the reusable public factory; do not relabel a union file as the supplied automatic annotation or claim its source QC certified physical occupancy.

Bind original S/T/D and derived occupancy separately, retain source-label counts, and make the derived flag honest in task extent/provenance. NativeSpatialCase currently emits occupancy_modified=false unconditionally in the supplied-goal record; a union must not inherit that claim.

Freeze baseline access across the pair and verify full T/D/source MRI unchanged. Existing admission can only be reused if bindings distinguish acquired annotations from the simulated occupancy assumption; no truth-valued source/QC fields may be forged.

Focused generated controls: exact unchanged baseline identity; union adds exactly T minus S and is idempotent; unchanged T/D/full denominator; unknown domains not expanded; fixed access/tools/geometry; SELECT and EVAL refusal; forged derived provenance refusal. No controls have been run for this recipe.
interpretation: A change from STOP to progress supports sensitivity to the occupancy interpretation under these fixed tools and access; it does not validate S union T anatomically. Continued STOP leaves action/access/reward and algorithm limitations unresolved. Historical raw TRAIN and zero-shot SELECT results remain the original baseline; new TRAIN findings do not authorize retrospective SELECT retuning.
